outline: The course will introduce students to basic conceptual frameworks and analytical tools used in investment analysis, and then to apply them to a variety of standard and nonstandard applications.  The primary objective of this course is to help prepare students to work as finance professionals in a variety of positions.  Some of the material may be useful for analyzing personal financial objectives.
schedule:
Introduction
•	What is finance, who does it help, why should you care, who else cares? (BKM 1)
o	Financial instruments: variety, uses (BKM 2)
o	How securities are issued and traded (BKM 3)
•	Pricing review
o	Discounted cash flows (DCF): interest rate risk adjustments, cash flow expectations (Review your intro finance course notes)
o	Price ratios: equities, anything with comparables available (BKM 18)

Hedging
•	Introduction to payoff diagrams and linear payoffs (BKM 22)
•	Forwards/futures/swaps (BKM 23)
o	Applications

Diversification: Risk Measurement and Management
•	Mean-variance portfolio selection models (BKM 6-8)
o	CAPM and APT (BKM 9, 11)
•	Mean-variance risk measurement
o	Value-at-Risk
•	Advanced portfolio selection: optimal allocation considering endowed capital
o	Human capital considerations for private investors
o	Integrated risk management for the Firm
o	Measuring and managing country risk
•	Risk measurement for non-traded securities and portfolios: tracking portfolios, CAPM/APT benchmarking (BKM 10)
•	Performance measurement and management
o	Sharpe ratio, CAPM or factor model alpha, others (BKM 24)

Financial Insurance: Options
•	Introduction to options and nonlinear payoffs (BKM 20)
•	Binomial model: arbitrage pricing of derivatives, risk measurement (BKM 21)
o	Decomposition and Recomposition of Risks: Arrow Securities as Building Blocks
•	Black-Scholes option pricing: Greeks and implied volatility
•	Applications
o	Firm Valuation using option pricing (Merton model)
o	Credit Risk: Risky Debt and Credit Derivatives
o	Underwriting versus synthesis approach to financial product creation
o	Executive stock options: cost to the firm and value to recipient
	Compensation system design: incentives and retention
o	Prepackaged trading strategies using custom derivatives
o	Government-sector risks: deposit insurance and pension guarantees

Risk Accounting and Corporate Management
•	Off balance sheet transactions (BKM 19)
o	Defined-benefit and defined-contribution pension plans: influence of taxes
o	Defined-benefit pension plans: risk and limitation of traditional accounting
o	Swaps
